content.tldr: Iceberg executes ACID MERGE and UPSERT operations using either Copy-On-Write (rewriting matching data files) or Merge-On-Read (writing delta and delete files).
content.simple_explanation: Executing a SQL MERGE joins the target Iceberg table with incoming staging records to classify rows into matched updates and unmatched inserts. In Copy-on-Write (CoW) mode, Iceberg rewrites every target data file containing a modified row, generating clean new Parquet files. In Merge-on-Read (MoR) mode, Iceberg writes newly inserted rows to new data files and writes deleted/updated rows to separate positional delete files, leaving original data files untouched until compaction.
content.real_world_example: Updating an encyclopedia entry: Copy-on-Write reprints the entire volume page with corrections; Merge-on-Read places an errata sticker over the old sentence and appends new paragraphs in an addendum.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: CoW produces optimal query scan performance for analytics but creates high write amplification during streaming updates. MoR minimizes write latency but shifts merge overhead to query time.
